Title: PM CARES' Delayed Accounts Raise Questions over Missing ...
URL: https://www.moneylife.in/article/pm-cares-delayed-accounts-raise-questions-over-missing-audit-report-notes-and-325-crore-refunds/81454.html
Published: N/A
Author: N/A
Highlights:
The PM CARES Fund has made its financial statements for FY23-24 and FY24-25 public, with the latest disclosure raising questions about the availability of the accompanying audit report and notes, as well as a ₹324.66 crore refund received from implementing agencies. The one-page receipts and payments account for FY2024-25 carries references to an accompanying auditor’s report and notes 1 to 16, but these are not part of the document available on the fund’s website.

The accounts for the year ended 31 March 2025 were signed by officials of the PM CARES Fund in New Delhi on 6 August 2026 and by chartered accountant Tejas Parikh, partner at Mumbai-based KKC & Associates LLP, on 7 August 2026, more than 16 months after the close of the financial year, transparency activist Commodore (cmde) Lokesh Batra (retd) points out.
...
The FY23-24 accounts have also been released alongside the FY24-25 statement. The PM CARES website now lists audited receipts and payment accounts for both financial years, with FY22-23 having been the latest year for which an account was previously available on the website.

The PM CARES website’s FAQ states that no statutory period is prescribed under the Income Tax Act for auditing the fund’s accounts. It also states that the fund is audited by an independent auditor and that KKC & Associates LLP, Mumbai, has been appointed as its auditor for three years.
...
Interest earned on fixed deposits amounted to ₹469.38 crore, while interest on savings bank accounts was ₹5.77 crore. The statement also records ₹324.66 crore as ‘refund from implementing agencies’, compared with ₹84.31 crore under the same head in FY2023-24.

The fund received total receipts ... ,279. ... 1 crore during ... , including donations, ... income, refunds from implementing agencies and ... on fixed-deposit interest. Against this ... 5 lakh. ... lakh was spent
...
The receipts and payments account carries the statement: “Accompanying notes to the financial statements - 1 to 16.” It also states: “As per our report of even date attached.”

The one-page document available on the PM CARES website, however, does not contain the accompanying notes or the auditor’s report referred to in the statement. The absence of the accompanying notes has been highlighted by transparency activists Anjali Bhardwaj and Cmde Batra.

Ms Bhardwaj has questioned why the notes referred to in the financial statement were not uploaded along with the account. She also sought details of the ₹324.66 crore refunded by implementing agencies, including which agencies returned the money and the purpose for which the original payments had been made.

The ₹324.66-crore entry in the FY24-25 statement carries a reference to note 11. The one-page statement itself does not identify the implementing agencies concerned or provide details of the transactions covered by the refund.

Cmde Batra has separately drawn attention to the absence of the accompanying notes and the auditor’s report from the documents available on the PM CARES website. He has also pointed out that the FY23-24 and FY24-25 accounts carry signatures dated 6th August and 7 August 2026.

The FY24-25 statement has been audited by KKC & Associates LLP, formerly Khimji Kunverji & Co LLP. The PM CARES website states that the trustees appointed KKC & Associates LLP as the fund’s independent auditor for three years.

The PM CARES website currently lists receipt and payment accounts marked as audited for FY19-20 through FY24-25. The latest accounts for FY23-24 and FY24-25 were signed in August 2026, while the financial year covered by the latest statement ended on 31 March 2025.

Title: PM CARES Fund Audit Raises Questions on Transparency
URL: https://frontline.thehindu.com/politics/pm-cares-fund-audit-transparency-questions/article71373611.ece
Published: 2026-08-22T00:00:00.000Z
Author: Soni Mishra AI Summary
Highlights:
When the latest audit statements of the Prime Minister’s Citizen Assistance and Relief in Emergency Situations (PM-CARES) Fund were released on its website on August 18, they revealed a corpus that had grown to a record high since its inception in March 2020. Eyebrows were raised about the minuscule expenditure, and it led to renewed demands for greater transparency in the donations received by the fund and the spending made from it.

The “Receipts and Payments” accounts of the fund, released after a gap of two years and covering the financial years 2023-24 and 2024-25, reveal that the fund’s balance had grown to Rs.8,452 crore as on March 31, 2025. The closing balance for 2023-24 was Rs.7,173 crore. Overall, the corpus grew by Rs.1,279.9 crore, from 2023-24 to 2024-25. According to the audit report for 2022-23, the fund had Rs.6,283 crore.
...
Out of the Rs.7,173 crore at the beginning of 2024-25, Rs.6,641.56 crore was kept in fixed deposits, while Rs.531.46 crore was held in savings bank accounts, and this resulted in interest earnings of around Rs.475 crore. A refund of Rs.324 crore is listed as having been received from implementing agencies.
...
The account statements were signed by the independent auditor KKC & Associates LLP, Chartered Accountants, who were formerly known as Khimji Kunverji & Co LLP, and dated August 7, 2026. Four government officials of the ranks of Secretary, Director, Under Secretary, and Section Officer, signed the statements on behalf of the fund. Until 2022-23, the audit reports of the fund were prepared by SARC & Associates, Chartered Accountants.
...
Questions have been raised about why there is no detailed information on the refund of Rs.324 crore that is listed in the statement for 2024-25. “With regard to the amount refunded, there are no details about which authority refunded the large amount and for which purpose that amount was disbursed,” Batra said.

He also pointed out that the accompanying notes to the audit reports, which are specified by the auditor in the reports as totalling 16 pages, have not been uploaded.

“Why were the reports delayed by two years? And then, they cannot be considered audited reports because they only provide a statement of receipts and expenditure. The auditors’ observations in ‘Accompanying notes to the Financial Statements’ are not reflected in these reports. Also, while as per the PM CARES fund portal, auditors were to be changed after three years, the last auditor went on for four financial years,” Batra said.

Title: ₹8,452 Crore in Bank, ₹88 Lakh Spent: PM CARES Opens Two Years of Books at Once | Times Now
URL: https://www.timesnownews.com/india/8452-crore-in-bank-88-lakh-spent-pm-cares-opens-two-years-of-books-at-once-article-155754929
Published: N/A
Author: N/A
Highlights:
The PM CARES Fund has released two years of accounts in a single stroke. Its receipts and payments statements for 2023-24 and 2024-25 were both signed off in the first week of August 2026 — by the fund's officials in Delhi on 6 August and by its auditors in Mumbai on 7 August. For the 2023-24 accounts, that is more than two years — about two years and four months — after the financial year closed on 31 March 2024.
...
picture finally arrived, it showed a fund that ... spending almost entirely. In 2023-24, PM CARES paid out ... ₹15.6 crore — nearly all of it, ₹15.4 crore, on the PM CARES for Children scheme. In 2 ... 24-25 it spent even less: ₹87. ... 5 lakh in total, of which ₹87. ... 4 lakh went ... the Children scheme and ₹451 ... bank and SMS charges. That is ... per cent of the money
...
The money itself kept piling up. PM CARES closed 2024-25 with ₹8,452 crore, up from ₹7,173 crore a year earlier. Most of it is now locked away: ₹7,846 crore sits in fixed deposits with banks, with another ₹605 crore in savings accounts. Those deposits are working hard — the fund earned about ₹475 crore in interest in 2024-25 alone, more than 500 times what it spent. On top of that, donors still gave close to ₹480 crore during the year, and implementing agencies returned ₹324.66 crore of earlier allotments, with no breakdown in the statement of which agencies sent it back or why.

Both delayed years were signed by a new auditor, KKC & Associates LLP, formerly Khimji Kunverji & Co, which replaced SARC & Associates, the firm that had audited every year from 2019-20 to 2022-23. The change of auditor and the clearing of two years' worth of accounts in one week point to a backlog settled all at once.

The timing sits awkwardly against how the fund is set up. Donations to PM CARES qualify as corporate social responsibility spending under the Companies Act, 2013, and for full tax exemption under Section 80G; foreign donations are accepted under a special FCRA window. The Prime Minister is the fund's ex-officio chairman, and the defence, home and finance ministers are its ex-officio trustees. A fund chaired by the Prime Minister, run by senior Union ministers and financed entirely by public, corporate and foreign donations took more than two years to show donors an audited statement — while continuing to maintain that it is not a "public authority" answerable under the Right to Information Act. The government has defended that position in affidavits before the Delhi High Court, where the question is still being litigated.

It placed orders with companies that had no prior experience in making ventilators. Only two of the seven companies – Skanray, whom government-run Bharat Electronics Limited collaborated with, and Allied Medical Limited – had any substantial track record of manufacturing critical care ventilators.

In contrast, AgVa and Jyoti CNC, with negligible experience, got orders of 10,000 and 5,000 units respectively.

Media reports claiming that Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY beneficiaries who are already dead are still on the system getting treatment are misleading, the health ministry said on Thursday. The ministry also said that mobile numbers have no role in deciding beneficiary eligibility. The ministry's remarks came in response to media reports that claimed that the Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG) has flagged that treatments have been booked for AB PM-JAY beneficiaries who have been declared dead on the system. The reports also claim that the same beneficiary had been found to avail treatment at two hospitals at the same time. "These media reports are completely misleading and ill-informed," the ministry said. 

 The CAG report which contains results of the Performance Audit on Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri - Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY) covering the period September 2018-March 2021 was placed in parliament in the Monsoon Session of 2023, the ministry said in a statement. "It is clarified that under AB PM-JAY, hospitals are allowed to initiate requests for pre-authorization up to three days post the date of admission in the hospital. This feature is enabled to avoid denial of treatment in case of limited connectivity, emergency situations, etc," the statement said.
...
In some cases, the patients were admitted and before their pre-authorisation was raised, they died. 

 "In such cases, the date of death is the same as the admission date or earlier. Moreover, death has also been reported by the same hospital which raised the pre-authorization request. Thus, had the hospital intended to defraud the system, it would not have shown any interest in declaring the patient dead on the IT system," the statement said. 

 It is pertinent to note that more than 50 per cent of cases highlighted in the report have been booked by public hospitals, which have no incentive in committing fraud, as the money is reimbursed in the hospital account, it said. Further, in case of death during treatment, the hospital has to mandatorily submit a mortality report, it said. There are also many instances where the patients were admitted in the hospital as private patients (self-paid) but when they discovered the scheme, they requested the hospital to register them under the scheme for free treatment, the statement said. The feature that allows back-dated pre-authorisation helps save people out-of-pocket expenditure. On the patient getting treatment in two hospitals at the same time, the statement said that under AB PM-JAY, children up to 5 years of age avail treatment on the Ayushman Card of their parents. Accordingly, Ayushman Cards can simultaneously be used for children and either of parents at two different hospitals, it said. Usually, mother and child avail treatment using one Ayushman Card only, and if the child dies during treatment, the hospital declares the child dead which erroneously gets registered against the card of the mother, the statement said. Subsequently, when the mother comes for next treatment, she is denied services on the grounds of her Ayushman Card being marked as 'dead.' In such cases, grievances are raised, and the 'dead flag' against the card of mother is removed, it said. The government said it has deployed a four-step robust claim processing system under AB PM-JAY with the veracity of the hospital's claims examined at each step, the statement said. It said defined triggers are run on claims to identify cases which need further examination. Such cases undergo desk and field audits and in case a hospital is found to be committing any fraud or abuse, penal actions including de-empanelment are initiated against the erring hospital. The CAG finding one mobile number associated with multiple beneficiaries has no operational and financial implications as beneficiary identification process under Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY is not linked with the mobile number, the ministry said. "The mobile number is captured only for the sake of reaching out to the beneficiaries in case of any need and for collecting feedback regarding the treatment provided," the statement said. Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY identifies beneficiaries through Aadhaar identification. "The details fetched from the Aadhaar database are matched with the source database and accordingly, the request for Ayushman card is approved or rejected based on the beneficiary details. Thus, there is no role of mobile numbers in the verification process," the statement said. The AB PM-JAY caters to a beneficiary base (bottom 40 per cent) where many of them may not possess a mobile number or keep changing it frequently, it said. Accordingly, the NHA has provided three additional options, i.e. fingerprint, iris scan, and face-authorisation for beneficiary verification along with OTP, of which fingerprint-based authentication is most used. In view of the above, treatment to the beneficiaries can't be withheld just on the grounds that the beneficiary doesn't carry a valid mobile number, or the mobile number given by them has changed, the statement said. "Accordingly, beneficiary mobile numbers have a very limited role in the AB PM-JAY treatment workflow. Also, the fact that PM-JAY is an entitlement-based scheme and not an enrolment-based scheme and therefore, the beneficiary database is fixed and cannot be edited to add new beneficiaries. "Thus, mobile numbers have no role in deciding beneficiary eligibility. Therefore, it is an erroneous presumption that beneficiaries can avail treatment using mobile number," the statement stated. The ministry also argued that since there was a field that asked for mobile numbers, it is possible that some random ten-digit number was entered by the field level workers in some cases in the earlier stages of the scheme implementation. The OTP-based validation was not on initially as many beneficiaries either didn't carry the mobile with them or they shared the number of their relative or neighbour. The ministry in the statement said that the National Health Authority and Ministry of Health and Family Welfare are examining in detail the recommendations of CAG performance audit report and necessary action is being taken to make the system more "robust, efficient and prudent."
